original: ἵνα τί τὸ πρόσωπόν σου ἀποστρέφεις ἐπιλανθάνῃ τῆς πτωχίας ἡμῶν καὶ τῆς θλίψεως ἡμῶν
translation: Why do you turn your face away? You forget our poverty and our affliction.
differences_from_web: LXX 'turn away your face' where WEB has 'hide your face'
LXX 'our poverty' (πτωχία) where WEB has 'our affliction'; 'oppression' is rendered 'affliction' (θλῖψις)
LXX has no 'and' linking two questions; the verse opens with ἵνα τί 'why' once
_web_text: Why do you hide your face, and forget our affliction and our oppression?

original: ἵνα τί, Κύριε, ἀφέστηκας μακρόθεν; ὑπερορᾷς ἐν εὐκαιρίαις ἐν θλίψει;
translation: Why, Lord, have you stood far off? Do you overlook us in times of need, in affliction?
_web_text: Why do you stand far off, LORD? Why do you hide yourself in times of trouble?

original: Ἕως τίνος, Κύριε, κράξομαι, καὶ οὐ μὴ εἰσακούσῃς; βοήσομαι πρὸς σὲ ἀδικούμενος, καὶ οὐ σώσεις;
translation: How long, Lord, shall I cry out, and you will not listen? I shall shout to you when wronged, and will you not save?
literal_notes: εἰσακούσῃς: aorist subjunctive with οὐ μή, 'you will not listen'
differences_from_web: LXX 'when wronged' (ἀδικούμενος) where WEB has the cry 'Violence!'
_web_text: LORD, how long will I cry, and you will not hear? I cry out to you “Violence!” and will you not save?

original: ἀπὸ τῆς ταλαιπωρίας τῶν πτωχῶν καὶ ἀπὸ τοῦ στεναγμοῦ τῶν πενήτων νῦν ἀναστήσομαι, λέγει Κύριος· θήσομαι ἐν σωτηρίᾳ, παρησιάσομαι ἐν αὐτῷ.
translation: Because of the misery of the poor and the groaning of the needy, now I will arise, says the Lord. I will set him in safety; I will speak freely in him.
differences_from_web: LXX final clause 'I will speak freely in him' differs from WEB 'from those who malign him'
_web_text: “Because of the oppression of the weak and because of the groaning of the needy, I will now arise,” says the LORD; “I will set him in safety from those who malign him.”

original: ἐν θλίψει ἐπεκαλεσάμην τὸν κύριον, καὶ ἐπήκουσέν μοι εἰς πλατυσμόν.
translation: In affliction I called upon the Lord, and he listened to me, leading me into spaciousness.
literal_notes: εἰς πλατυσμόν: 'into a broad place / spaciousness'
differences_from_web: LXX 'he listened to me into a broad place' vs WEB 'answered me with freedom'; close in sense
_web_text: Out of my distress, I called on the LORD. The LORD answered me with freedom.
